news_communities.title: Former Melrose High School soccer player set to play in the World Cup, for Haiti
news_communities.author: Oscar Margain
news_communities.summary:
A Massachusetts soccer player is getting ready to play for Haiti in the World Cup after helping the team qualify for the tournament for the first time in 52 years.

Frantzdy Pierrot, who played at Melrose High School, moved from Haiti to Massachusetts when he was 11.

“Me playing my first game in Boston means a lot to me,” Pierrot told NBC10 Boston. “It’s like a second World Cup.”

Growing up in Haiti, Pierrot said life often felt uncertain. He said the love from his parents and his passion for soccer gave him stability while he spent his childhood playing soccer with few resources.

“You just play on the streets, and our toes would be bleeding because we’d be kicking rocks,” Pierrot said. “So when I finally got here, I was about to wear shoes, or like, seeing the soccer ball, I was like ‘wow.'”

Pierrot joined youth sports in Medford before playing soccer at Melrose High School, where he met coach Dean Serino.

“He’s the first one that was like, ‘You got something special,'” Pierrot said. “Just him saying that to me made me believe that I can actually do anything.”

Serino said Pierrot’s determination separated him from other players.

“It was his determination that you knew he was going to be great. I knew he was. He was bound for great things, I just didn’t know this great,” Serino said.

Pierrot went on to play at Northeastern University before turning professional. At 31, he now plays soccer in Europe and led Haiti to the World Cup after scoring a qualifying goal against Costa Rica last year.

“I know that I’m giving a lot of people in my country hope,” Pierrot said.

He added that he wanted the people who helped him throughout his journey to feel proud as they watched him compete at the highest level.

“They’re all going to be witnessing me playing on one of the biggest stages, and they can say, ‘This kid, I helped him,'” Pierrot said.

Haiti will face Scotland on June 13 at Boston Stadium. Pierrot will be recognized by Gov. Maura Healey in a proclamation on Tuesday.

news_communities.title: Chelsea plans '39-day party' for World Cup, but still awaits FIFA license
news_communities.author: Oscar Margain
news_communities.summary:
UPDATE (Tuesday, May 26, 2026): The city tells NBC10 Boston that its FIFA license has been approved.

With 20 days remaining before the start of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the city of Chelsea, Massachusetts, moved ahead with plans for a 39-day celebration despite still waiting for approval to show tournament matches publicly.

City officials launched promotional campaigns for watch parties, soccer events and family activities planned throughout the tournament. Leaders said they expected the World Cup festivities to bring tourism dollars to local businesses while encouraging residents to gather in public again.

Chelsea City Manager Fidel Maltez noted 70% of the city is comprised of a Latino population, and 53% are foreign-born. He said immigration enforcement activity over the last year had hurt businesses and kept many residents from spending time downtown.

“We walked our streets in fear. We felt like we couldn’t come outside. Our business owners complained about how our downtown was decimated,” he said.

Maltez said the city hoped large public gatherings and increased local police presence would help residents feel safe during the tournament.

“Anytime that there was a large gathering, [ICE] shied away from it,” he said.

The city has planned several English and Spanish watch parties in Chelsea Square and other activities tied to the World Cup.

Beginning June 11, Chelsea Square will be transformed into an outdoor gathering space for the tournament. Visitors can expect an outdoor large-screen viewing experience, local food vendors, music and community programming showcasing the cultures and traditions of the city’s diverse community.

Chelsea Sports Tourism Director Charlie Giuffrida said officials wanted to create opportunities for local families and youth soccer players during the tournament.

“We want to make sure our youth soccer ecosystem and all of our community has some amazing things to do to capitalize on what’s going to be, probably, one of the best summers North America’s seen in a long time,” said Giuffrida.

Maltez said the city allocated nearly $500,000 in combined state and local funding for the celebrations.

However, organizers said they still had not received FIFA licensing approval to broadcast matches during public watch parties.

“It’s definitely scary that we’re weeks away and we don’t have a license yet,” said the city’s civic designer, Omar Miranda, who applied for a license several months ago.

Several other cities and towns hosting World Cup watch parties were also still waiting for FIFA approval, including Worcester, Brockton, Everett and Lexington.

Even if the license does not arrive in time, organizers said the city still planned to move forward with festivities.

“They’re going to watch it in our businesses if they have to. We’re just going to have a space for them to have fun and enjoy the celebrations,” said Miranda. “Licenses or not, we’re going to have a 38-, 39-day party here at Chelsea Square.”

The City of Chelsea posted a watch party calendar on its website and is kicking off “Fiesta Fútbol” on Saturday with other public activities to follow:

  • Adult Soccer Tournament: 10:30 a.m. Saturday, May 23, at Highland Park, 45 Willow Street, Chelsea
    The City is accepting 16 teams for an 8v8 double-elimination tournament. Teams are encouraged to play as their home or favorite nations — including Honduras, El Salvador, the United States, Mexico, and others — and wear culturally-themed gear. Pre-registration is required at recreation.chelseama.gov.
  • Soccer Field Day — Youth Soccer Community: 10:30 a.m. – 2:30 p.m. Saturday, June 6 at Highland Park, 45 Willow Street, Chelsea
    Open to the entire Chelsea Youth Soccer Community, Soccer Field Day will feature mini soccer matches, a skills competition, inflatables, local vendors, and more. Families can learn about local soccer programs and register on-site. No pre-registration required.

All are welcome, including those who attended private, vocational, or other schools. Players register by graduating year or decade and are grouped accordingly. Games are continuous 7-v-7 format beginning at 10 a.m.

news_communities.title: Annabelle is moving to Salem
news_communities.author: Mary Markos
news_communities.summary:
One of the most infamous dolls in the world is officially coming to Salem, Massachusetts.

The allegedly haunted Annabelle doll, made famous by paranormal investigators Ed and Lorraine Warren, will be part of a new exhibit opening on Essex Street in Salem later this summer.

The announcement came during a livestream walk through downtown Salem by YouTuber Elton Castee and comedian Matt Rife, who now oversee the Warrens’ collection.

Where will the Annabelle exhibit be in Salem?

Castee gave NBC10 Boston an exclusive in-person look at the exterior of the location.

“The part of the building we have is all the way to that corner there … that building … This! Right here!” he said, pointing out the Essex Street space.

The exhibit will take over roughly 4,000 square feet, with plans for around 1,000 to 1,500 artifacts tied to the paranormal and occult history.

The temporary museum is expected to open Aug. 26 and could run through the fall, possibly staying until just before Christmas.

What is the Annabelle doll?

Annabelle is widely known from paranormal investigations and horror films, but its origins trace back decades.

“It is a demonic doll that posed to be this Annabelle Higgins’ spirit,” Castee explained.

According to the Warrens, the doll was believed to be possessed and was ultimately locked away for safety. It has since become one of the most recognizable items in their collection.

Warren Museum collection expanding to Salem

Castee and Rife took over stewardship of the Warren Occult Museum collection in Connecticut and say bringing artifacts to Salem has been months in the making.

“It’s been a process — we’ve been working on this for eight, nine months in Salem alone,” Castee said.

The exhibit will go beyond just Annabelle, featuring a wide range of items connected to:

  • Paranormal investigations
  • Occult history
  • Famous historical cases
  • Cultural beliefs about the supernatural

“We’re not just bringing a few haunted items here,” Castee said. “We’re curating something really expansive.”

Their goal, he says, is to educate visitors — something inspired by the Warrens themselves.

“I want people to leave this experience and be like, ‘We saw Annabelle, but also, I want to look up more about this tribe, or this belief, or these people, or what is this?’ and just leave people with more curiosity than they came in with,” Castee said.

Salem residents react to Annabelle’s arrival

In a city known for its connection to the 1692 Salem Witch Trials and thriving paranormal tourism scene, reaction to Annabelle’s arrival has been mixed — but largely enthusiastic.

“We live in Salem — we’re downtown — this is why we’re famous,” one resident said.

Others say the exhibit fits perfectly with the city’s identity.

“I’m scared — but I feel like it’s also kind of intriguing,” a visitor said.

But there are residents who have raised concerns about late-night crowds.

Museum hours and community impact

City leaders have approved temporary operating hours, allowing the museum to stay open:

  • Until 11 p.m. Sunday through Thursday
  • Until midnight on Fridays and Saturdays

Those hours could be revisited later this year.

Castee says he and his team plan to live in Salem and want to integrate into the community.

“We want to be a part of this community,” he said. “If there’s anything that we can figure out to make things better, please let us know.”

When can you see Annabelle in Salem?

If all goes as planned, visitors will be able to see the Annabelle doll and the expanded exhibit starting late August of this year.

“Now is the time to take action. Our youth are dying right in front of us, and what are we doing to stop it?” Gilliard asked. “What do we have in place? What alternative do we have? Now is the time.”

“We know, overall, the numbers continued to follow a downward trend, and that the statistics this year, to date, actually are a decrease compared to last year,” Mayor Michelle Wu of Boston’s violent crime statistics.

Still, the mayor said that there is work left to be done, any that act of violence is unacceptable.

news_communities.title: Teen charged in Danvers murder appears virtually in court
news_communities.author: Staff Reports
news_communities.summary:
A teenager charged with the murder of a woman in her home in Danvers, Massachusetts, appeared virtually in court Monday.

Anthony DeMayo, 18, of Lynn, is accused of breaking into the home of 68-year-old Janet Swallow on March 12 and stabbing her to death.

DeMayo pleaded not guilty in March to charges of murder and armed home invasion in Salem District Court. He was ordered to undergo mental evaluation at Bridgewater State Hospital.

He remained at the hospital Monday when he was arraigned at Essex Superior Court. While he acknowledged being able to hear the court proceedings, his attorney asked for a plea of not guilty to be entered on his behalf due to questions of competency.

The investigation that led to DeMayo’s arrest began after a 911 caller told police that a man was acting erratically, walking around on Standish Road in Lynn with what looked like a blood-stained knife. Officers responded and found DeMayo, taking him to Salem Hospital.

DeMayo reportedly told Lynn police that he had killed a woman the night before in Danvers.

A search of the Bishop Fenwick High School student’s Lynn home revealed blood-stained clothing, and along with data from his cell phone, investigators contacted the Danvers Police Department, who conducted a well-being check and found Swallow dead inside her home on Amherst Street.

Prosecutors said Swallow was found dead, alone, “suffering wounds consistent with a homicide.” They said DeMayo apparently entered the home by climbing through a window and stabbed Swallow while she was in bed. They said no items were found to be missing from the home and they believe the attack was random.

The longtime Danvers resident was an ICU nurse at Lahey Hospital in Burlington and leaves behind two sons.

Scott James, Lahey’s chief nursing officer, called Swallow “a beloved and valued member of the Lahey Hospital & Medical Center community” who will be “greatly missed.”

“We share our deepest condolences with her family and loved ones and her colleagues in the Nursing Department and across our hospital. Our thoughts are with them during this very difficult time,” he added.

Officials said there is no known connection between DeMayo and Swallow.

DeMayo remained held without bail after Monday’s superior court hearing.

A status hearing is scheduled for May 29.

news_communities.title: Fallen Trooper Kevin Trainor's mother: ‘I just remember screaming for my son'
news_communities.author: Robert Goulston
news_communities.summary:
The grieving mother of fallen Massachusetts State Police Trooper Kevin Trainor visited the barracks where he worked to spend time inside his cruiser on Monday, days before his funeral.

Barbara Trainor said the cruiser covered in flowers was her son’s police cruiser for the first few years on the job. She wanted to spend time in it before it was moved.

“It just made us feel a connection to him,” said Trainor. “Try to see what he was going through every day. One of the troopers explaining everything to us, which was really nice.

Trooper Trainor was killed early Wednesday morning while responding to a report of a wrong-way driver on route one in Lynnfield. The Essex County District Attorney’s office says the wrong-way driver hit Trainor’s current cruiser head-on. Both Trainor and the other driver were killed.

“It just keeps replaying in my mind over and over and over. How he was almost there and he would be here today,” Trainor said in an interview.

Trainor’s mother said she got the phone call minutes after it happened: “I got a call in the middle of the night and I answered the phone. I just literally blacked out. I just remember screaming for my son.”

Trainor says she will never forget that knock on the door, “and saw them on my porch. I knew what that meant and I just collapsed. Literally collapsed.”

More on the death of Trooper Kevin Trainor

Massachusetts State Police May 7

Trooper Trainor’s funeral Mass will be at the same church in Salem where he just gave the eulogy for his father back in March.

“We remember now in a moment like this to honor those who bravely put themselves in danger for our safety,” said Father Bob Murray, pastor at Mary, Queen of the Apostles Parish in Salem.

Murray will also preside at Trooper Trainor’s funeral Mass on Wednesday.

“His sense of what it meant to serve and to be a man at the beginning of his career, to serve with the Middlesex sheriff and then to move on to the state troopers,” said Murray.

Trainor’s mother said she knows her son and his father are together and knows her son’s spirit will live on.

“Nothing I can even say about that. Constant sadness. I miss my son,” Trainor said.

Trooper Trainor’s original cruiser has been moved from outside the barracks to be prepared for the funeral arrangements later this week. The wake is scheduled for Tuesday and funeral on Wednesday.

news_communities.title: State trooper dies after wrong-way crash that closed Route 1 north in Lynnfield
news_communities.author: Kaitlin McKinley Becker
news_communities.summary:
A Massachusetts State Police trooper died from his injuries after his cruiser was struck by a wrong-way driver, who also died, on Route 1 in Lynnfield early Wednesday, officials said.

State police confirmed the trooper’s death, saying they did so was with deep sadness and condolences to the trooper’s family, classmates and loved ones.

Gov. Maura Healey said she was heartbroken by the trooper’s tragic death, that her thoughts and prayers were with his family, loved ones and fellow state police members during this incredibly difficult time.

“The Trooper was responding to reports of a wrong-way driver and put himself in harm’s way to protect others,” Healey wrote in a statement. “This act of service and courage is what our State Police are called to do every day. They show up ready to face danger so the rest of us can be safe. Today, Massachusetts is mourning one of those heroes.”

State police identified the trooper at a press conference outside the Danvers barracks as 30-year-old Kevin Trainor, a trooper of three years who represented “the best of the best.” A procession was held for him in the South End, as fellow first responders saluted as his body was taken by.

Click here for more comments about Trainor from the press conference

State police said earlier Wednesday that the trooper had been rushed to a Boston hospital with life-threatening injuries after his cruiser was struck around 2 a.m. by a driver who was traveling south in the northbound lanes on Route 1 northbound.

Trainor’s shift was scheduled to end at 2 a.m., according to state police. The 911 call reporting a wrong-way driver came in at 2:01 a.m., and Trainor’s cruiser was struck head-on at 2:04 a.m.

The wrong-way driver, identified by Essex County prosecutors as Hernan Marrero, a 50-year-old Roslindale resident, died at the scene, while Trainor succumbed to his injuries at Massachusetts General Hospital.

“While nothing will ever repair the pain we feel today, we make a solemn promise to never forget Trooper Trainor and his service to the Commonwealth,” Col. Geoffrey Noble said in a statement. “Make no mistake: Trooper Trainor saved lives this morning. His courage – his commitment to serve the citizens of the Commonwealth and put his life on the line – prevented an even greater tragedy. He will be remembered as a hero.”

“We will remember and honor this extraordinary man, son, fiancée, and friend who gave his life for others,” Noble continued.

The Massachusetts Department of Transportation announced Route 1 northbound was closed at Walnut Street in Saugus due to the crash, and traffic was being detoured.

Drivers were told to seek alternate routes, and anyone traveling through the impacted area was warned to expect delays, MassDOT said. Closures lasted several hours.

news_communities.title: New details revealed on Saugus home invasion where gunshots were fired

Prosecutors revealed new information on Sunday’s armed home invasion in Saugus, Massachusetts, as the suspects appeared in court Monday.

Derek Matarazzo and Timothy Gregory are charged with multiple charges including home invasion. Matarazzo is also charged with assault with a dangerous weapon and discharging a firearm.

On Tuesday in Lynn District Court, both suspects were ordered held without bail pending a dangerousness hearing.

Police say the two men who were dressed all in black armed with gun, and then when they arrived at the home, the two men were found in the yard. Gunshots were fired, but no one was hurt.

Prosecutors say both men were out of breath and Matarazzo was asking if the other suspect was okay.

“Making statements about potentially going to jail for 30 years and asking officers if his friends was dead or shot,” said Essex Assistant District Attorney Kaitlyn Bastarache said.

The police reports were impounded until after a grand jury hears the case, but the prosecutor indicated in court the men were after safes in the house and that the attempted robbery was caught on video.

“There is mention of surveillance video in the home that was broken into, in the bedroom in which items were taken, has video from inside the home as well,” Bastarache said.

Several people were in court on behalf of two suspects. One woman would only say she was a friend of Matarazzo’s family.

“He made a few mistakes. His family is behind him. They are working really hard to get him back,” said the woman. “He is going into really work through this and his friends and family are all behind him.”

We did talk to one person who was in the home at the time of the incident. He said they were all shaken up and there was a young person in the home at the time. But made it clear he did not want to be identified or do an interview at this time.

A woman was injured after jumping from the second story of a burning building in Everett, Massachusetts, on Friday, fire officials said.

The fire was reported around 11 a.m. on Franklin Street. When firefighters arrived, they found fire in the rear hallway of the building going up to the second and third floor.

Fire officials said they received a report that someone was still trapped inside on the second floor, but she jumped out a window before firefighters were able to extend a ladder to her. She suffered a head injury and was taken to an area hospital. No update on her condition was immediately available.

Neighbor Billy Hurley Jr. said he saw the woman leaning out of the window, with thick black smoke billowing around her. After hesitating, she made the jump.

“Either you’re gonna live or you’re gonna die, so she jumped out the window and she missed a fence,” Hurley said, adding he “could hear the thud of it.”

Everyone else made it out of the building safely, officials said. Fifteen residents were displaced in all.

Two firefighters suffered non-life-threatening injuries while battling the fire.

The fire took about an hour to extinguish, and the cause remains under investigation. State Fire Marshal’s Office investigators also responded to the scene.

“I’m a lifelong neighbor on the street, all my family’s been on the street over 107 years, so it was sad to see the whole house that’s been around … catch on fire and there’s so many people displaced,” Hurley said.

news_communities.title: State Ethics Commission alleges misconduct by former Everett Mayor Carlo DeMaria
news_communities.author: Glenn Jones and Mike Pescaro
news_communities.summary:
The former mayor of Everett is facing renewed scrutiny from the Massachusetts State Ethics Commission.

Last February, Massachusetts Inspector General Jeffrey Shapiro found that then-Mayor Carlo DeMaria had erroneously received an extra $180,000 in longevity payments.

DeMaria, who served 18 years as mayor, lost his reelection bid to new Mayor Robert Van Campen in November in the wake of the scandal.

The State Ethics Commission opened an investigation earlier this month and said Wednesday that it had found DeMaria violated the state’s conflict of interest law.

“DeMaria violated § 23(b)(2)(i) by using his official position as Mayor of Everett to conceal his receipt of unauthorized and inflated longevity payments, which was an unwarranted privilege of substantial value not properly available to similarly situated individuals, and he did so repeatedly and continuously while mayor,” the commission wrote.

Shapiro’s office said that before the ordinance granting longevity payments was approved in 2016, a subtle tweak was made to its language: Instead of saying the mayor would receive $10,000 “after each completed full term as mayor,” as it previously did, it was amended to read “for each completed full term as mayor.”

Ultimately, DeMaria was overpaid by $180,000, Shapiro said.

An independent audit later found DeMaria had received an additional $30,000 in improper funds.

The former mayor has not been penalized for the payments.

NBC10 Boston reached out to DeMaria for comment. He has previously denied any wrongdoing.

The State Ethics Commission is authorized to impose a civil penalty of up to $10,000 for each violation and may also order restitution payments. It will schedule a hearing within 90 days.

news_communities.title: 2 arrested in Everett bank robbery as Boston police investigate 2 more
news_communities.author: Matt Fortin, Asher Klein and Mike Pescaro
news_communities.summary:
A bank was robbed in Everett, Massachusetts, hours after two other bank robberies in Boston Tuesday, and two people have been arrested, police said.

Everett police initially said the suspects taken into custody after the robbery of Eastern Bank at the intersection of Broadway and Ferry Street, shortly after 4:30 p.m., matched the description of the two being sought by Boston police. They later said the people who were arrested were not the same ones wanted in the Boston crimes.

A Boston police representative previously said the department was aware of the arrests in Everett, but didn’t know of any confirmed connection.

Police have not identified the two people who were arrested.

On Tuesday morning, police in Boston said two separate robberies occurred in Roxbury and Roslindale, and that the same people were believed to be responsible for both crimes.

“Both of today’s robberies are very active investigations. Preliminary information gathered by detectives indicates both robberies involve the same suspects,” Boston Police Sgt. Detective John Boyle said in an email after the second robbery.

No injuries were reported in either case.

Everett police later responded to the robbery at Eastern Bank. They said a female robbed the bank before meeting up with a male and walking up Broadway and onto Gledhill Avenue, where police stopped them.

A gun and a machete were recovered, police said.

Boston police had released surveillance images from the two robberies in that city as they searched for the robbers.

The first robbery occurred at a Santander Bank branch on Washington Street in the Nubian Square area, and photos showed someone brandishing a gun at a teller about 10:11 a.m.

The two male robbers inside the bank wore blue face masks, blue gloves, hoodies and black pants. Police said they ran off along Harrison Avenue toward Orchard Park, and might have been in a blue Toyota RAV4 with Massachusetts license plate 4MXN78.

The second robbery was reported around 11:55 a.m. at a TD Bank branch on American Legion Highway. Two people robbed the bank at gunpoint, stealing an undisclosed amount of money, then ran out to a waiting car being driven by a third person. They drove off toward Cummins Highway, police said.

The first suspect is described as a male wearing a black hoodie, black pants, a black face mask, white and black sneakers, and blue gloves. The second suspect is described as a male wearing a black Champion hoodie with white lettering, black pants, and a black face mask.

As with the first incident, the suspects fled the scene in a blue Toyota RAV4 with Massachusetts license plate 4MXN78.

news_communities.title: Road rage fight caught on camera in Lynn
news_communities.author: Oscar Margain and Matt Fortin
news_communities.summary:
A man was hospitalized after a road rage incident Friday morning in Lowell, Massachusetts.

The incident escalated into an assault at a car wash on Route 1A. It’s being investigated by Massachusetts State Police, who responded shortly before 9:30 a.m..

Video from the scene showed traffic at a standstill as several people got out of their cars and started fighting in the roadway.

Two men were seen throwing punches while others tried to break it up.

A third man can be seen knocking someone to the ground.

“People have an ego,” said Jay Lopez, a customer at the car wash. “When somebody doesn’t back down, they have like, ‘Oh, I’m not going back down either.’ And then they just have to go back and forth until somebody goes to sleep.”

He feared it could have gone worse.

“It could have been a gun,” he said. “All you’ve got to do is mind your business. Drink water, mind your business.”

State police said the man who was knocked down suffered a laceration. He was taken to an area hospital.

No arrests have been made.

news_communities.title: Chelsea High School teacher on leave after allegations of inappropriate behavior
news_communities.author: Griffin Gonzalez
news_communities.summary:
A high school teacher in Chelsea, Massachusetts, has been placed on leave after allegedly having inappropriate conversations with students.

Parents and students say the inappropriate behavior went on for years. The district took action after students staged a walkout at Chelsea High School this week.

“For the past three years, I’ve been enduring a teacher who has been inappropriate towards myself and other students,” 17-year-old Jelannie Hunter told the Chelsea School Committee this week.

“When you’re working with children, there are boundaries,” her mother told NBC10 Boston in an interview Thursday.

She said she went to the school for the past three years complaining of the teacher’s conversations with her daughter.

Students at Chelsea High School walked out of class Wednesday to protest the lack of action taken by the district despite complaints from students and parents.

“As of today, the employee involved has been placed on leave,” Chelsea Public Schools said in a letter to the Chelsea High School community Wednesday. “The school district has also initiated an independent investigation of the concerns raised regarding this matter.”

The district also said in the letter that while it “encourages and supports students’ constitutional rights to freedom of speech and expression,” it planned to discipline some students who stayed in the halls longer and “and disrupted the instructional day for themselves and others who did not participate.”

NBC10 Boston is not naming the teacher, as no charges have been filed against her.

We reached out to the district to see whether or not she would be paid throughout her leave and why action was taken now after years of complaint, but have not received a response.

news_communities.title: As Artemis II crew splashes down, Navy sailor from Mass. was set to greet them
news_communities.author: Thea DiGiammerino
news_communities.summary:
A U.S. Navy sailor from Massachusetts was expected to be among the first people to greet the Artemis II astronauts when they returned to Earth Friday evening.

Chief Hospital Corpsman Vlad Link is a member of the dive medical team that was set to open the Orion capsule, the U.S. Navy said in a media release. Link, who is from Chelsea, was expected to help get the astronauts out of the capsule safely after splashdown and make an initial medical assessment of their condition.

Link has 18 years of experience in dive medicine.

“I have been exposed to the Navy since I was a young teenager, and I’m proud to represent both my family and hometown,” Link said in the media release. “Contributing our efforts to NASA and the Artemis II mission is something we take great pride in as part of that legacy.”

NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Christina Koch and Victor Glover and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen returned to Earth on Friday evening after 10 days in space. This involved a fiery plunge through the atmosphere, ending in a splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego.

news_communities.title: Teen held without bail on murder charge in Chelsea stabbing
news_communities.author: Mike Pescaro, Marc Fortier, Griffin Gonzalez and Sebastian Agudelo Gomez
news_communities.summary:
A teenager has been charged with murder in connection with a deadly stabbing on Thursday night in Chelsea, Massachusetts.

Sergio Josué Castellanos, 18, was held without bail at his arraignment Friday. He was allowed to hide his face in court.

Police responded to the intersection of Chestnut Street and Everett Avenue around 6:45 p.m. Thursday, and said multiple people were injured in stabbings.

Authorities said Friday that two people were injured: Castellanos, who suffered minor injuries, and 25-year-old Eduardo Rózales López of Chelsea.

Prosecutors with the Suffolk County District Attorney’s Office said López was treated at the scene for stab wounds to his neck and torso. He was transported to Massachusetts General Hospital, where he died from his injuries early Friday morning.

Reviewing video, police described seeing five people chasing after López. A man identified as Castellanos could be seen striking López in a stabbing motion while he’s on the ground, prosecutors said.

The video allegedly showed Castellanos and three other people fleeing. Police found him and three other males behind the fence of a home nearby on Chestnut Street.

Castellanos, who was tending to a stab wound to his leg, had changed his clothes from those seen on camera, which were found next to him, prosecutors said. He was transported to an area hospital for treatment.

Authorities said a black machete with stains on the blade was recovered.

Castellanos’ defense attorney, asking that his client be released on bail with GPS monitoring, raised questions about the identity of the attacker. He noted that in the video in which prosecutors described Castellanos making a stabbing motion, no knife was seen.

The judge ordered Castellanos held without bail.

Family members told Telemundo Nueva Inglaterra that López arrived from Guatemala seven years ago and leaves behind a 2-year-old child.

People in the area were shocked by the confrontation.

“It was kind of scary, I’m not going to lie. You still see the remnants of blood on the floor,” neighbor Shauniece White said Thursday. “It’s extremely concerning. As you see, it’s only been one nice day so far. If it’s already happening now, I can only imagine what the summer has in store for us. I’m hopeful that the police will come out and do due diligence to keep the community safe, but wishful thinking in a time like this.”

Massachusetts State Police are assisting Chelsea police with the investigation.

news_communities.title: Danvers murder suspect was spotted wandering around Lynn before his arrest
news_communities.author: Amelia Fabiano
news_communities.summary:
A young man raised alarm on Thursday as he wandered streets and backyards in Lynn, Massachusetts, carrying a knife. Neighbors who saw him were shocked to learn that he’s accused in a murder in Danvers.

Multiple people told NBC10 Boston that they saw 18-year-old Anthony DeMayo walking around at about noon Thursday with a large knife in his hand. Later, he would be identified as the suspect in the murder of Janet Swallow in Danvers.

Several of them called 911, which led police to arrest him in a backyard on Standish Road. The whole thing was caught on home surveillance video.

“They said they saw a crazy guy with a knife, and I’m like, ‘How did this happen,’ you know? It’s scary, you never think, where you live, it’s going to happen,” John Bossi said.

Security cameras captured the moments leading up to the arrest. It starts with a vehicle crashing into Nells Pond in Lynn around 11:40 a.m.

“It’s hard to even get there. I don’t know how he got through. There’s no easy way for a car to get there,” Bossi said.

About 13 minutes later, DeMayo is seen walking down Bow Ridge Road in a bright green shirt, swinging a knife around in his right hand.

Then, he goes to Nells Pond Road. Ashley O’Brien was outside with her ducks when she saw him walk by.

“I thought for sure that this guy was obviously mentally unwell. I didn’t want to make a scene and run away or anything like that, cause he made eye contact with me,” she said.

She immediately called 911, the first of several calls from the neighborhood.

“I just waited till he passed my house, went in, told my husband and called the cops,” O’Brien said. “When we came back out, he was just kind of stabbing all the bushes outside and running a knife across the houses and stuff like that — it was very bizarre.”

Rhonda Deparolesa was another on nearby Standish Road.

“I was sitting on my chair, in the recliner, and all of the sudden, I see somebody jump over my fence,” Deparolesa said. “He just laid flat on his back on the bulkhead and just wasn’t moving, so my husband was upstairs, and I said, ‘Something’s going on here.'”

Deparolesa said he tried to open her door at one point, but thankfully, it was locked.

“What if he did get in my house? My husband and I might not be here,” she said. “You know, you think you’re safe in your house. Sometimes you’re not.”

By around 12:30 p.m., police were after him. They found him in a backyard a few doors down from Deparolesa’s home. He was arrested and placed in a police cruiser.

“I’m just absolutely shocked that a young kid, 18 years old, had his whole life ahead of him, and had to go and do this,” Deparolesa said. “For what? Why?”

Everyone who spoke to NBC10 Boston was shocked to learn DeMayo is accused of murder.

“I just thought this guy needed some help and I just called. I did not think that he’d just murdered somebody,” O’Brien said.

Police confirmed DeMayo was a student at Bishop Fenwick High School in Peabody. They did not comment on the investigation, but said they are fully cooperating with local law enforcement.

Their thoughts and prayers are on the victim, her family, and everyone impacted by the horrific tragedy. They said their focus right now is on staff and students.

They had additional counselors on campus Friday and will on Monday, as well.

news_communities.title: New details revealed in court about Malden teacher accused of raping high school student
news_communities.author: Kaitlin McKinley Becker
news_communities.summary:
A 54-year-old teacher accused of raping a high school student in Malden, Massachusetts, faced a judge Thursday, a day after his arrest.

Authorities allege Scott Marino gave alcohol to an 18-year-old who is known to him and then sexually assaulted her last Wednesday, Feb. 18, at his Stoneham home, where the victim was currently living. Marino was arrested a week after the alleged incident and has been charged with two counts of rape, one count of indecent assault and battery and one count of furnishing alcohol to a person under the age of 21, according to the Middlesex County District Attorney’s Office.

Prosecutors provided shocking new details Thursday in Woburn District Court at the arraignment for Marino, who teaches at Linden STEAM Academy in Malden and coaches the girls’ basketball team at Malden High School.

Resources for victims of sexual assault are available through the National Sexual Violence Resources Center and the National Sexual Assault Telephone Hotline at 800-656-4673, and Massachusetts provides this list of statewide and resources for sexual assault survivors.

Jacob McCrindle of the Middlesex County District Attorney’s Office said in court that the alleged victim in this case had been in the foster care of Marino and his wife at the time this occurred. The victim, who moved in with the Marinos at their Stoneham home in the fall, was a basketball player for Marino during the season, and the two were known to each other for many years.

According to prosecutors, Marino’s wife was scheduled to take a trip out of state last Wednesday. The victim was on school vacation, so she went with Marino and a grandfather who lives in a basement apartment at the home to an Ash Wednesday mass. They dropped the older man off at home, and then Marino and the victim went driving because she had a learner’s permit and was learning to drive on the highway. They made the decision to go into Boston to get a takeout seafood dinner, and on the way home, Marino had them stop at a liquor store where surveillance video shows he purchased a strawberry margarita mix, a large bottle of Patron tequila and some other agave liquor.

The two then went back to Marino’s Stoneham home and he allegedly gave her a large margarita. She drank some of it but didn’t like it, though Marino allegedly encouraged her to keep drinking. He later poured them shots of tequila, and they ate the seafood dinner they got. The victim later told police that she was feeling ill so she went to her bedroom where she vomited many times, eventually lying down in bed.

Marino then came in and sexually assaulted her two times, prosecutors said in court. The victim later retrieved her cell phone and began texting friends and ultimately an aunt, begging for help.

McCrindle said that the aunt called 911 as she was driving to the Marino’s home, and the victim was taken to Winchester Hospital for a full sexual assault examination.

“This is a relationship where the defendant was the victim’s foster parent, he took her into his home, that’s a position of trust, as well as coupled with the fact that the defendant is a teacher, or was a teacher at the Malden Public Schools and he was also her coach for many years,” McCrindle said in court, arguing for $100,000 cash bail. “The defendant used I would suggest that relationship, he took advantage of that relationship, there’s a significant age difference, the defendant is 54 years old, the victim is 18 years old. There’s also a significant size difference that’s described in the police report between the defendant and the alleged victim…. it’s also noteworthy that the defendant appears to have waited until his wife left the home so he was more isolated with the victim…clearly some planning went into this.”

Marino’s defense attorney argued before the judge that he’s a respected educator with deep community support who has “never been in court in his life.”

The judge ultimately ordered $75,000 cash bail based on the gravity of circumstances along with several conditions requested by the commonwealth, including that Marino stay away and have no contact from the victim and any witnesses, stay away from all Malden school property and events, be fitted with a GPS bracelet to enforce exclusive zones including the victim’s home address, her school, her workplace and a gym that she frequents, surrender his passport and not be allowed to leave the state.

The judge also added the condition that Marino be alcohol free and submit to SCRAM testing.

Resources for victims of sexual assault are available through the National Sexual Violence Resources Center and the National Sexual Assault Telephone Hotline at 800-656-4673, and Massachusetts provides this list of statewide and resources for sexual assault survivors.

Malden Superintendent Timothy Sippel previously said the district was informed Wednesday that Marino had been taken into custody in connection with “a serious incident alleged to have occurred outside of working hours and involving one of our high school students.”

Marino was immediately placed on leave, the superintendent added, noting that the district is cooperating fully with law enforcement agencies in their investigation.

“I understand how upsetting and distressing this is to our community given the serious nature of these allegations,” Sippel said in a statement. “The safety of our students and staff is our highest priority.”

A plea of not guilty was entered on Marino’s behalf. He is due back in court for a probable cause hearing on April 16.

news_communities.title: Girl rescued after falling through the ice in Malden
news_communities.author: Thea DiGiammerino and Mike Pescaro
news_communities.summary:
Firefighters rescued a teen girl who had fallen through the ice into the frigid water of a pond in Malden, Massachusetts, on Wednesday afternoon.

It happened around 2 p.m. at Fellsmere Pond, fire officials said. Firefighters in water rescue suits went in to find the girl holding onto the edge of the ice, according to the Malden Fire Department. She was pulled from the water in under 30 seconds.

“I don’t even think the engine stopped,” Malden Fire Captain Roy Tribble said. “I jumped up, I sprinted down here, pretty much just jumped right into the water.”

The 14-year-old girl was conscious and alert when she was brought to a Boston hospital for treatment.

Tribble said the water was about 30 feet deep.

“A life was saved. It was a young girl who fell through the ice,” added Captain Bob Hegarty.

He warned everyone to stay off thin ice.

“A warning to everybody out there that ice, if it’s not thick enough, you’re going to fall through, and if you fall through, you’re not going to be able to get yourself out,” Hegarty said. “So stay off the ice until it’s very thick, which — who can tell when it’s very thick?”

news_communities.title: Malden woman accused of threatening federal agents making immigration arrest
news_communities.author: Thea DiGiammerino
news_communities.summary:
A Massachusetts woman is accused of threatening to kill federal agents who were conducting immigration enforcement in Malden.

Bethany Abigail Terrill, 37, was charged with threatening a United States official, the U.S. Attorney’s Office said Thursday.

Prosecutors say that Terrill approached the agents as they were making an arrest outside Malden District Court on Sept. 29, describing her as verbally abusive. She allegedly shouted things like “ICE is here, ICE is here,” “You guys are monsters, this is insane,” “Sir, what’s your name, what’s your name,” “I can try to help you,” and “I am an American civilian, I have a right to be here,” and called the agents Nazis.

She is further accused of trying to push past the agents, yelling “Charlie Kirk died, and we love it… We’re coming for you, gonna kill you.” 

According to the statement of probable cause, an agent heard the threat and proceeded to detain Terrill, who they said was “actively resistant and fought to escape.”

Officials say the agents were wearing body cameras, and Terrill was also filming at the time. In the statement of probable cause, investigators say the threat can be heard in the footage from Terrill’s phone.

The agents on scene were from multiple agencies, including Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), ICE and the FBI.

During her appearance in U.S. District Court in Boston on Thursday, a public defender said Terrill owns a salon and was struggling with legal issues in an unrelated case.

Judge Paul Levenson ordered Terrill be released with conditions, saying “federal agents have a right to not be subjected to threats.”

Terrill was ordered as part of her conditions of release to participate in a mental health program for treatment on a regular basis, to develop a safety plan for her own safety and others, avoid contact with potential witnesses, have no contact with any federal official, family or otherwise in any way or form, refrain from alcohol and the use of any illegal drugs, to avoid contact with law enforcement, and to refrain from making any further threats.

She didn’t speak to reporters outside of court.

The charge of threatening a U.S. official carries a sentence of up to 10 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of $250,000.

news_communities.title: Cities bordering Everett unite in Revolution soccer stadium transparency push
news_communities.author: Asher Klein
news_communities.summary:
Four cities that border Everett, Massachusetts, have banded together in a push for more involvement in the New England Revolution’s plans for a soccer-specific stadium in the city.

The mayors of Revere, Medford, Malden and Chelsea formed a coalition called City Mayors for Citizens that they said will seek transparency on plans for the stadium, including the impacts it will have on their communities.

The 25,000-seat stadium proposal has progressed in the state Legislature but still faces plenty of hurdles. The City Mayors for Citizens said they are worried about how the building on along the Mystic River might impact local infrastructure, public transit and quality of life.

“A project of this size and scale will have significant regional impacts,” said Revere Mayor Patrick Keefe Jr said in a statement. “We want to ensure that a stadium is contributing positively to the communities it is drawing resources from. Our residents should not bear the burdens of a private stadium that has strong potential to negatively affect their day-to-day lives.”

Asked for a response to the statement, a Revolution club spokesperson noted that it expects to work with neighboring communities after it reaches agreements with Everett and Boston, which would allow the property to have its port designation removed and the process of construction to continue.

The spokesperson also noted that the team thanked the mayors and promised to review the concerns raised in their letter, sent Monday.

news_communities.title: Video shows Salvadoran man being detained by ICE in Malden
news_communities.author: Oscar Margain, Marc Fortier and Mark Garfinkel
news_communities.summary:
The wife of a Salvadoran man says he was violently taken into custody by immigration officials on his way to work in Malden, Massachusetts, on Wednesday morning.

The incident occurred shortly before 6 a.m. in the area of 28 Kennedy Drive.

Leslie Perlera Gonzalez said she received a distressing call from her husband, Edgar Hernan Elias Escobar, shortly before 6 a.m. as he was heading to his construction job. She rushed to Kennedy Drive, where she said Elias Escobar was surrounded by immigration officers.

“I heard them smash his window, and he was saying, ‘Ow, you’re hurting me,'” Perlera Gonzalez said. “When I arrived on the scene, he had a Taser on his face.”

The 31-year-old had no criminal record and was in the process of adjusting his immigration status after the couple married last year, noted Perlera Gonzalez.

“He’s never come close to doing anything that would be considered a crime,” she said.

She alleged that agents used an unmarked car to ram her husband’s vehicle, forcing him off the road before detaining him.

Malden police said Elias Escobar sustained minor injuries. He was transported on a stretcher to a hospital in Melrose, where Perlera Gonzalez said she was not allowed to see him.

About an hour later, he was moved to a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement processing facility in Burlington.

A spokesperson from the Department of Homeland Security said in a statement that Elias Escobar was the target of the ICE operation and suffered “no injuries.”

“On September 17, 2025, ICE conducted an immigration enforcement operation in Malden, Massachusetts to arrest Edgar Hernan Elias-Escobar, an illegal alien from El Salvador. During the arrest, the illegal alien refused to comply with officer commands to rolldown his window. The officers took appropriate action and followed their training to use the minimum amount of force necessary to resolve the situation in a manner that ensured the success of the operation and prioritized the safety of the public and our officers,” the spokesperson said in a statement. “Out of an abundance of caution, ICE law enforcement escorted Elias-Escobar to the hospital for evaluations. Medical staff found he had no injuries and discharged him. He was then escorted to the Boston Filed office for processing and will be placed in removal proceedings.”

“I’ve been expecting this from somebody I know every day since Donald Trump was elected,” said Amiee Parco, an attorney with Greater Boston Legal Services and a colleague of Perlera Gonzalez. “I’ve been waiting for it to affect me personally.”

Friends and coworkers gathered outside the Burlington facility, joining a weekly protest to support Elias Escobar’s release and that of other detainees.

“He’s a really wonderful person,” said Alyssa Rao, a friend of the couple. “I think this is going to impact everyone.”

After Wednesday’s ordeal, Perlera Gonzalez fears what her husband is going through while detained.

“I’m terrified of what could be happening when no one is watching,” she said.

At last check, Escobar was still at the facility. It’s unclear how long he’ll be held — often, people stay several days, though the facility is meant to detain people for hours.

His lawyer is trying to prevent the government from sending him to a far-away detention center, and from deportation.

ICE has ramped up arrests across greater Boston in recent weeks under “Operation Patriot 2.0,” detaining immigrants in public spaces.

Gov. Maura Healey spoke out against the sweeps on Tuesday, saying federal immigration enforcement officers are “creating an incredible amount of fear and intimidation.”

“Some of it seems purposeful, to be honest. Why else are you parked outside a church? Why are you parked outside a community center?”

The governor said her office has received no information from ICE about who is being detained or why.

“This is not a furtherance of public safety,” she said. “In fact, it undermines public safety.”

Asked what she can do to protest White House policy, Healey said: “I join with other governors in urging the Trump administration, in the strongest possible terms, to change course.”

State House News Service contributed to this report.

news_boston.title: These are the brands most frequently impersonated by cybercriminals
news_boston.author: Ale Zimmermann and Bianca Beltrán
news_boston.summary:
Cybercriminals are using well-known brands to steal consumers’ personal and financial information.

According to a report by cybersecurity firm Check Point, Microsoft, LinkedIn and Google are the top three brands most frequently used by criminals in phishing attempts during the second quarter of 2026.

But it wasn’t the top three companies that caught the attention of cybersecurity experts.

“We’ve been tracking this for years, but for the first time, ChatGPT has entered the top 10 of the most impersonated brands,” said Jeremy Fuchs at Check Point.

Artificial intelligence tools are becoming a new target for scammers.

“We observed a number of fake — that’s the key word, fake — ‘payment failed’ emails … with the idea of redirecting the person to a page that’s actually built to steal your legitimate billing or credit card details,” Fuchs explained. “This is obviously just picking up in steam, and given where ChatGPT is in the lexicon, and how popular it is, and how popular it’s going to continue to be, this is just the tip of the iceberg.”

Tech companies topped the list of most impersonated sectors, with social media and banking not far behind. Companies like LinkedIn are continuing to be used by scammers to defraud victims.

“Even just using the name ‘LinkedIn’ is enough — people are always looking for jobs,” Fuchs said. “They’re maybe always open to hearing about jobs or just networking with people in their industry or communities. Getting a fake email from LinkedIn might be convincing enough for somebody to click and hand over their information.”

The whole point is to rush users in the moment. Whether it’s with a payment issue, security alert, or update needed — it’s all meant to make people click with urgency.

“You can click on a link and then all of a sudden bad stuff starts happening to your computer. But that’s not always the case,” Fuchs said. “Scams have evolved and so that even just clicking on the link is actually not dangerous. It’s what you do with it, right.”

A lot of phishing emails get blocked before they hit the inbox folder, but some might still filter through.

The best way to stay protected is by going to official website address and verifying the information before clicking any link.

“Hackers are really, really good at sort of playing off the news or different trends or the time of year to get people who are expecting emails from those companies,” Fuchs said. “Being sort of aware of where we are in the world and what’s going on and also what you’re doing online is crucial.”

news_boston.title: Man with illegal weapons in home, car arrested at Trump golf club in California
news_boston.author: Phil Helsel and Andrew Blankstein | NBC News
news_boston.summary:
A man with weapons in his home and vehicle who appeared to be “monitoring security-planning activities” at the Los Angeles-area Trump National Golf Club was arrested days before a planned presidential visit, the county sheriff’s department said Tuesday.

Jeanine John Taele, 38, a resident of the Los Angeles-area city of Downey, was arrested Sunday at the course in Rancho Palos Verdes, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department said.

The department said deputies found a loaded magazine with hollow-point bullets in Taele’s pants pocket after they’d been contacted by plainclothes federal agents regarding a suspicious person at 3:28 p.m.

“The individual was observed walking throughout the golf course grounds taking photographs and videos and appearing to monitor security-planning activities,” the sheriff’s department said in a statement.

The department said deputies arrived and made contact with Taele and learned he was under investigation for robbery in the Los Angeles-area city of El Segundo. They also found a loaded pistol in his vehicle at the club’s parking lot, officials said.

Taele was arrested on suspicion of carrying a concealed firearm and possession of armor-piercing or otherwise prohibited ammunition, the sheriff’s department said.

Taele’s home was searched Monday, and an “illegally modified AR platform rifle,” a .45-caliber pistol, body armor, high-capacity magazines and ammunition were found, the sheriff’s department said.

“Multiple notebooks containing concerning statements” and two “radio signal devices” were also discovered, the sheriff’s department said.

The arrest came two days before Donald Trump was scheduled to visit Los Angeles and have a fundraiser at the golf resort. The sheriff’s department did not mention any direct threat to the president.

Trump arrived by Marine One helicopter at the golf resort at around 5:07 p.m. local time Tuesday, according to pool reports.

Taele has been charged in connection with the 2025 robbery, as well as the incident that began Sunday, according to a criminal complaint.

Jail records showed Taele was in custody Tuesday. Online court records did not appear to show an attorney for him Tuesday evening, and efforts to find a phone number connected with him were not immediately successful.

He is charged with second-degree robbery and also three other counts that deal with possessing a large-capacity magazine, having a concealed firearm in a vehicle and possession of a short-barreled rifle, records show.

Rancho Palos Verdes is in the Los Angeles area but is a separate city on the Pacific coast, around 20 miles southwest of downtown Los Angeles.

In 2024, another man, Ryan Routh, was arrested in an assassination attempt on the president at the Trump International Golf Club in West Palm Beach, Florida.

Routh, who the Justice Department said was observed pointing an AK 47-style rifle from a “sniper’s hide” near a fence on the border of the golf course, was convicted in 2025 and sentenced to life in prison in February.

news_boston.title: Harlem Lacrosse introduces the sport to hundreds of Boston kids
news_boston.author: Malcolm Johnson
news_boston.summary:
For University of Mount Saint Vincent lacrosse player Naveah Martin, picking up a lacrosse stick changed the course of her life.

“When I first started playing lacrosse in middle school, I wasn’t really doing anything productive,” Martin said. “Harlem Lacrosse gave me something to do in the afternoons and allowed me to be with my friends. Then we started going to bigger cities and I began meeting new people.”

Martin is one of many former participants who credit Harlem Lacrosse with opening doors on and off the field.

The nonprofit organization, which combines year-round lacrosse programming with academic support, leadership development and mentorship, hosted a free summer clinic Tuesday for more than 300 children in Boston, many of whom were playing the sport for the first time.

Babson College lacrosse player Daivyon Williams also discovered the game through Harlem Lacrosse.

“The first time I touched a stick was in sixth grade and I fell in love with it,” Williams said.

Williams originally hoped to play football but found a different opportunity through lacrosse.

“I wanted to play football and I wasn’t good enough,” he said. “But as soon as I played lacrosse, it was different, and I knew it would be on a different path, but I could excel in it.”

Harlem Lacrosse Boston Executive Director Patrick Cronan said introducing young people to the sport is about more than learning the game.

“Coming out here, you can just tell with the amount of smiles everywhere you look,” Cronan said. “Even the kids that were a little bit defensive and had their guard up and might’ve been too cool to try something new — everyone’s smiling and having a good time. There is something there for everyone.”

The organization was founded about 15 years ago by Massachusetts state Rep. Simon Cataldo, who was teaching special education in Harlem at the time.

“None of my students had played an organized sport before,” Cataldo said. “We went down with a whistle and a clipboard. About 15 years later, this thing is happening all across the country now.”

Cataldo said the organization’s impact extends well beyond athletics.

“Our students are now earning well over $150 million in academic scholarships,” he said. “Our kids are in Ivy League schools and community colleges.”

Massachusetts state Rep. Christopher Worrell, who partnered with Harlem Lacrosse to host Tuesday’s clinic, said exposing children to new activities is especially important.

“Making sure our kids have access to something new and getting them outside of the house is important,” Worrell said. “Every year we try to make sure kids enjoy themselves and experience something they’ve never played before. You hear the laughter — it was amazing.”

Organizers hope the clinic inspires the next generation of players, just as it did for Martin and Williams, whose first experiences with the sport eventually led them to compete at the collegiate level.

news_boston.title: Seawall repairs at stake after FEMA grant for Rockport is canceled
news_boston.author: Brianna Borghi
news_boston.summary:
A long-planned project to repair the seawall at Long Beach in Rockport, Massachusetts, is facing an uncertain future after the Federal Emergency Management Agency canceled nearly $2.8 million in funding.

The seawall has stood for about a century, but residents say it has become increasingly vulnerable to storms and rising tides.

“I don’t know what will happen once we get a really good storm because the wall is failing,” Long Beach resident Lisa Mooney said.

Mooney’s family has had a home at Long Beach for generations. She said the seawall is critical to protecting the cottages along the shoreline.

“There definitely is a rise in the tides and a need for a better support for the seawall here to protect all these homes,” Mooney said.

Rockport voters had already approved the town’s required share of the project, which would have allowed the town to access the federal grant. The FEMA funding was expected to pay for repairs to portions of the wall that had already been damaged in previous storms.

Antoinette Giugliano, a member of the executive committee of the Long Beach Improvement Association, said the project should not be viewed as a political issue.

“This has nothing to do with whether I’m Republican or Democrat, it only has to do with fixing something that seriously and desperately needs repair,” Giugliano said.

Without the federal funding, supporters say it will be difficult for Rockport to move the project forward.

“Rockport is a small town and to absorb a cost like that would be difficult. So we were depending on that FEMA grant money, and to take it away from us just really seems wrong,” Giugliano said.

The town owns the land at Long Beach, while residents own the homes located there. Supporters of the repairs say those properties generate millions of dollars each year in lease payments and property taxes that help support the town and its schools.

The seawall also helps protect nearby marshes, estuaries and other coastal habitat from storm damage.

FEMA’s decision could also affect previously approved projects in six other coastal Massachusetts communities, including Gloucester, Hull, Marshfield, Nahant, Scituate and Quincy.

Gov. Maura Healey is urging FEMA to reverse the decision.

If the cancellation stands, affected communities could lose funding they have counted on for years. Some could also be required to repay federal money already spent on planning, engineering and design work, potentially shifting those costs to local taxpayers.

news_boston.title: ‘Game of Thrones' author George R. R. Martin opens up about experiencing depression
news_boston.author: David K. Li | NBC News
news_boston.summary:
George R. R. Martin, author of the wildly popular “Game of Thrones” book series, shared that he’s pulled back from updating fans via his blog as he “battled sadness and depression.”

“This year has been… stressful, to say the least,” Martin wrote in a blog post published this week, titled “Better Late Than Never.” “So much has been happening, it’s been overwhelming. Some great things, exciting things. Dreams coming true. But there have been nightmares too. I have lost friends. Battled sadness and depression.”

The entry marked Martin’s return to blogging since since Feb. 19. In his latest post, he thanked his “great staff of assistants,” who he said have worked tirelessly to keep him from “falling further and further behind.”

In recent years, the fantasy author has been called out by readers who complain about the delayed publication of the sixth “Game of Thrones” book, “The Winds of Winter.”

Martin addressed the criticism last year, writing in a May 2025 post that he “ought to get some other writer to pinch hit for me… I am going to die soon anyway, because I am so old. I lost all interest in ‘A Song of Ice and Fire’ decades ago. I don’t give a s— about writing any longer, I just sit around and spend my money.”

In Monday’s post, Martin referenced his age again, writing, “The worst may be yet to come. I turned seventy-seven last September, and I tell you, getting old is no fun.”

He told fans that the combination of age and depression could mean his “posts are likely to [be] short and rushed” in the immediate future, adding that his “minions” may be helping him more.

But 2026 hasn’t been all sadness for the author, he said. In his post, he highlighted the nine Emmy nominations bestowed on his “A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms” on HBO Max.

Martin has won four Emmys, all as co-executive producer for “Game of Thrones.” The show won Emmys for outstanding drama series in 2019, 2018, 2016 and 2015.

This year’s awards show, which will air on NBC, takes place on Sept. 14 in Los Angeles.

“I hope to attend…” Martin wrote, “but that depends on… well, on a lot of things.”

news_boston.title: Healey will sign immigrant protections into law Wednesday
news_boston.author: Colin A. Young | State House News Service
news_boston.summary:
Gov. Maura Healey will sign a new immigrant protection measure into law Wednesday in Chelsea, saying the compromise bill Massachusetts lawmakers sent her last week “provides the strongest protections in the country against abuses by ICE, including keeping them out of courthouses, schools and hospitals.”

Lawmakers attached an emergency preamble to the bill, declaring it “an emergency law, necessary for the immediate preservation of the public safety” and arranging for it to take effect as soon as Healey signs it.

The bill (H 5620) that cleared the House and Senate on split votes last Thursday would expand protections against warrantless civil immigration arrests to courthouses, public schools, child care centers and healthcare facilities. It bars new agreements allowing state and local officials to perform certain federal immigration enforcement functions, preserves the Department of Correction’s existing partnership with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and codifies the Supreme Judicial Court’s 2017 Lunn v. Commonwealth decision which held that there is “no authority for Massachusetts court officers to arrest and hold an individual solely on the basis of a Federal civil immigration detainer.”

“We started this effort by grounding our work in the belief that all Massachusetts residents deserve equal protection under both the United States constitution and Massachusetts constitution regardless of where they were born or their color, creed, or immigration status,” Sen. Cindy Friedman said Thursday before the Senate adopted the proposal. “And I would add that every single person in this Commonwealth, state, country, world deserve to be treated with dignity and respect. Nobody is illegal.”

Friedman said the bill was a response to ICE, an agency that she said “has become violent, frequently disregarding the law, and often seems to revel in sowing fear and division.”

Joining Healey for the 9:45 a.m. signing ceremony at La Colaborativa on 6th Street in Chelsea will be Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll, Education Secretary Steven Zrike, Office of Refugees and Immigrants Executive Director Cristina Aguilera-Sandoval, Chelsea City Manager Fidel Maltez, La Colaborativa President & CEO Gladys Vega, public safety officials, advocates and others.

Healey said the bill was “top of mind” for her last week and expressed hope it would reach her desk.

news_boston.title: Rangers hosting 10 Texas shelter dogs for Bark at the Park night
news_boston.author: Eric Mullin
news_boston.summary:
A group of Texas shelter dogs are getting to enjoy a night out at the ballpark.

The Texas Rangers are hosting 10 dogs from Irving Animal Services for Bark at the Park Tuesday night as the MLB club faces the San Francisco Giants.

The shelter pets are among hundreds of dogs expected to be in attendance at Globe Life Field in Arlington. A select number of fans were able to purchase theme night tickets allowing them to bring their dog to the game.

But the Rangers also provided complimentary tickets to the shelter dogs, along with the Irving Animal Services’ staff and volunteers who escorted the canines during their night out.

“We hope this special opportunity helps these shelter pets connect with future families and find the loving homes they deserve,” said Karin Morris, Rangers senior VP of community impact and executive director of the Rangers Baseball Foundation, in a statement.

The shelter dogs range in age from an 8-month-old pointer/terrier mix named Runner to an 8-year-old German shepherd mix named Osa. And the baseball game won’t be the dogs’ only special experience this week, either.

Adam Goldberg, co-founder of Stronger Shot Adoption Photos, held a photo shoot with the pets Monday. Stronger Shot aims to help shelter animals make a stronger first impression to prospective pet parents through professional photography and videography.

“I always say we have amazing dogs available for adoption—and while that may sound biased, it’s absolutely true,” said Egan Dobson, outreach coordinator for Irving Animal Services, in a statement. “These dogs are loving, smart, and so deserving of a second chance.”

“I’m excited not only for them to enjoy such a fun night out, but for people to see just how special shelter dogs truly are.”

The Bark at the Park event comes just days after NBCUniversal Local’s Clear The Shelters kicked off its 12th annual adoption campaign. Irving Animal Services is a founding Clear The Shelters participating location; the shelter in 2014 was part of an adoption led by NBC 5 DFW and Telemundo 39 Dallas that inspired the nationwide campaign.

Irving Animal Services saw 182 adoptions during last year’s Clear The Shelters campaign. The 2026 adoption campaign is being held for the entire month of August, while the donation campaign runs through Sept. 15.

“These shelter dogs have been through a lot, so we wanted to give them a great experience to kick off Clear The Shelters in a unique way in the heart of the campaign’s North Texas birthplace,” said Meredith McGinn, NBC Local’s executive VP of diginets and original production, in a statement.

This story originally appeared on NBCDFW.com.

For more information on Clear The Shelters, including participating shelters, along with details on local events and television programming, visit ClearTheShelters.com and the Spanish-language site DesocuparlosAlbergues.com. Follow Clear The Shelters on Facebook, Instagram and TikTok.

news_bc.title: Boston College Names Corey Kelly Vice President for Student Affairs
news_bc.author: Willy Connors
news_bc.summary:
Corey Kelly, associate vice president and dean of students, was named Boston College’s next vice president for student affairs, effective Aug. 1.

“Kelly brings extensive leadership expertise in student outreach and support, campus engagement, student conduct, and restorative practice, among other critical areas,” the University release of her appointment read.

Kelly succeeds Shawna Cooper Whitehead, who departed in May to serve as president of Regis University in Denver, Colo.

Unlike Cooper Whitehead, who was tapped for the role in 2021 after serving as vice president of student services at Seton Hall University, Kelly has spent her entire 13-year career under BC’s Division of Student Affairs. 

“She is credited with helping to establish a culture of care and accountability in Student Affairs, creating student experiences that enhance belonging and wellbeing, and addressing student behavior and mental health challenges consistent with the formative values of a Jesuit, Catholic university,” the release said of Kelly.

Kelly previously served as the assistant and associate dean of students and director of student conduct, and, most recently, associate vice president and dean of students.

In an email to The Heights, Kelly wrote that her years of experience have grounded her in “the University’s mission and shared commitment to a campus community where students experience belonging, growth, and care.”

She earned her bachelor’s degree in psychology and statistics from Boston University in 2009, and then continued her education at BC, earning a master of social work degree in 2013, and completing her Ph.D. in the Lynch School of Education and Human Development in 2019.

For her doctoral dissertation, Kelly published an extensive analysis of the challenges facing administrators handling campus sexual assault (CSA) cases, and called out flaws within the current system.

“Title IX Coordinators are at the forefront of this broken multi-layer system involving the government, individual institutions, and the administrators who are charged with managing CSA,” she wrote. “This needs to change in order for universities to be able to better respond to this important problem of CSA that is plaguing campuses nationwide and to improve the safety of all students while also respecting the rights of all students.”

Her dissertation is just a preview of the challenges she’ll have to address in her new role. 

Kelly also inherits a long-running fight over LGBTQ+ student resources on campus. Despite a decades-long push for a distinct resource center, one remains absent at BC.

In 2023, after renewed momentum under Cooper Whitehead, the University incorporated LGBTQ+ resources into the Thea Bowman AHANA and Intercultural Center (BAIC), but not without pushback that temporarily halted the initial plan.

University President Rev. Jack Butler, S.J., who also assumed his role on Aug. 1, all but ruled out a standalone center at BC. 

It’s unclear how Kelly will approach these challenges, but throughout her transition she has framed her leadership around continuity and care.

“The staff in our Division bring so much expertise and intentionality to their work with students and collaboration with colleagues, and I feel fortunate to have the opportunity to lead a group of such dedicated professionals,” Kelly wrote. “Looking toward the new academic year, I am eager to connect with students and work together to grow the caring culture that makes BC so special.”

As of publication, the University has not announced Kelly’s successor, and the Dean of Students position remains vacant.

news_bc.title: Bob Thompson Steps Down, Francesco D’Agostino Named Interim Head Coach Five Days Before Season Begins
news_bc.author: Mac Cobb
news_bc.summary:
Boston College men’s soccer head coach Bob Thompson is stepping down, according to a statement from BC Athletics released on Monday. Associate head coach Francesco D’Agostino has been named interim head coach. 

“After a lot of prayer and conversation with my family, I’ve made the difficult decision to step away from Boston College,” Thompson said, per the release. “My time here as a coach has been one of the most rewarding experiences of my life, but right now I need to be there for my family.”

Thompson’s decision comes five days before the Eagles are set to begin their season with an exhibition game at Northeastern. D’Agostino is familiar with the program, however, and is entering his seventh season on BC’s coaching staff. 

“I have complete confidence in the culture we’ve built, the character of our players, and in Coach Francesco’s ability to guide this group forward this season,” Thompson said. 

Thompson was named BC’s head coach in January of 2020 after spending two years as an associate head coach and serving as interim head coach in 2019. The Eagles finished the 2025 season 7–9–1, with a 1–6–1 ACC record. 

Since taking over as the permanent head coach, Thompson’s teams went 28–40–20, with a 5–23–12 record in ACC play. BC’s best year under Thompson came in 2024, when the Eagles went 6–5–6 and beat No. 8 North Carolina. Thompson’s lone postseason victory came as interim head coach, when the Eagles earned a 3–0 victory over Yale in the 2019 NCAA Tournament. 

Thompson also served as an assistant coach and recruiting coordinator for the Eagles from  2012–14 and spent time on coaching staffs at UMass Lowell, Tufts, and Northeastern. 

Thompson was a star player for BC men’s soccer from 1999–2002, receiving an honorable mention All-American in 2002 and winning the Big East Tournament MVP twice. His teams won two Big East Tournament titles, made three NCAA Tournaments, and set a school record for single-season wins with 18. Thompson went on to spend two seasons in the MLS playing for the New England Revolution.
